articleTitle: GreenFit: Renewable Energy and Interactive Entertainment
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Control, Automation, and Instrumentation (IC2AI)
abstract: Renewable energy is a booking technology nowadays where several engineering applications are centralized on such technique. However, integrating sports, gaming, and renewable energy in a full system has not been developed so far. Therefore, this paper proposes the GreenFit, a renewable energy and interactive entertainment system. This novel smart trainer comprises two interconnected components that combine electrical power generation and engaging gaming experiences. Firstly, the system focuses on renewable energy generation during physical activities. A generator installed on the bicycle captures the electricity generated by pedaling, creating a self-sustaining source of green energy. This eco-friendly approach not only encourages sustainable practices but also involves users directly in the energy generation process during their workouts. Secondly, the Smart Trainer features an interactive gaming interface, enhancing the fitness experience. Equipped with sensors that respond to the user's pedaling, the connected game behaves in real-time to match the workout's pace and intensity. The virtual environment reacts instantly to user movements, including braking, steering, and moving left or right, providing an immersive and responsive gaming experience. To sum up, this research paper focuses specifically on the development and evaluation of the GreenFit system, highlighting its innovative integration of renewable energy and gaming. Testing and validation yield in very good results.

articleTitle: Enhancing Epidemic Early Warning Systems with Social Media Data
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Control, Automation, and Instrumentation (IC2AI)
abstract: Early warning systems (EWS) play a crucial role in controlling the spread of infectious diseases. This study focused on the integration of social media data within artificial intelligence (AI)-based EWS for improved disease detection and monitoring. We conducted a scoping review to analyze the use of social media data in conjunction with AI-based EWS, aiming to identify the benefits, challenges, and key considerations for developing such systems. Our review examined various studies that employed machine learning models to analyze social media data for public health surveillance. The findings highlight the potential of social media data in enhancing the accuracy, efficiency, and responsiveness of EWS, enabling earlier detection of disease outbreaks and facilitating timely public health interventions. This review provides valuable insights for practitioners, researchers, and policymakers on the integration of social media data within AI-based EWS, contributing to the design and implementation of effective public health surveillance systems.

articleTitle: Improved Object Detection Through a Learning-Based Joint-Initiative Supervised Autonomy (JISA) Framework
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Control, Automation, and Instrumentation (IC2AI)
abstract: Object detection is faced with accuracy and robustness limitations due to unstructured environments with objects of different sizes and occlusions. Despite advancements in object detection models, these models have not reached a point to possess a comparable level of perception to humans, thus limiting their ability to effectively address challenges in diverse environments. Hence, adopting a human-in-the-loop approach in autonomous systems can handle complex perception scenarios. To tackle these issues, the Joint-Initiative Supervised Autonomy (JISA) framework is used to allow a human supervisor to intervene once the agent is uncertain of its predictions based on its self-confidence (SC) metric, or when the human deems the prediction incorrect based on his/her situation awareness (SA). However, the existing JISA framework formally defines the levels of autonomy between the human and the agent, but does not provide a means for learning from human interventions. In this paper, we present an enhanced version of JISA in object detection applications by implementing a learning scheme that is inspired by the Interactive Corrections and Reinforcement for an Epistemic and Aleatoric uncertainty-aware Teaching (ICREATe) algorithm. To address these challenges, we evaluate the results of the proposed framework and demonstrate that the model effectively learns and improves its performance through human feedback.

articleTitle: Hybrid Attention-Based Residual Network for Image Classification
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Control, Automation, and Instrumentation (IC2AI)
abstract: Residual Attention Networks (RANs) are a class of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) that integrate attention mechanisms into deep architectures. RANs employ stacked attention modules to generate attention-aware features from low-resolution images and map them back to the original feature maps. This synergistic approach leverages the strengths of CNNs and attention mechanisms, leading to enhanced image classification performance. In this study, we propose an improved RAN architecture by replacing the single-type attention mechanism with a hybrid attention mechanism. The use of two distinct hybrid attention mechanisms is anticipated to further improve the CNN-based model's performance.

articleTitle: SolaClean: An Autonomous Robot for Optimized Solar Panel Cleaning
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Control, Automation, and Instrumentation (IC2AI)
abstract: This paper presents the development of an automated solar panel cleaning robot aimed at addressing the inefficiencies and practical challenges associated with manual cleaning in large-scale solar energy systems. The robot integrates a lightweight aluminum bridge with wheeled legs that traverse parallel rails mounted on the panels. It features a centrally mounted four-wheel car chassis, a microfiber wiper on an aluminum rod, and a water-spraying nozzle. The system is powered by lithium batteries and managed by an Arduino Mega, interfacing with various sensors and a Bluetooth module for communication with a mobile application. The software supports user control for initiating cleaning cycles, monitoring the robot's status and water levels, and receiving alerts for low water or emergencies. The operational process involves spraying water, moving forward while wiping, automatically stopping water flow upon reaching panel limits, and returning to the parking position, with autonomous obstruction handling. Extensive testing confirms that the robot meets all requirements, providing a reliable and efficient solution for maintaining solar panel performance.

articleTitle: Study of PV Systems Integration on the Lebanese Grid
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Control, Automation, and Instrumentation (IC2AI)
abstract: This project will be focused on the effect of private level solar systems on the EDL grid, specifically on the distribution part of the entire EDL network. In order to show the said effects of the integration of solar panels into the EDL network, we created models using “power world simulator” to visually represent the changes and modifications happening in the network, in addition to the motion of power through the lines.

articleTitle: Adaptive Pure Pursuit with Deviation Model Regulation for Trajectory Tracking in Small-Scale Racecars
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Control, Automation, and Instrumentation (IC2AI)
abstract: Designing motion controllers for autonomous racecars allows researchers to study the safety and computational efficiency of their algorithms under extreme conditions, while also serving as a benchmark for conventional autonomous driving technologies. Small-scale autonomous racecars compel developers to use feeble processors or microcontrollers that are incapable of executing computationally-expensive control algorithms, like Model Predictive Control (MPC), in real time. On the other hand, geometric controllers are derived from kinematic models, where the steering angle is computed based on simple trigonometric equations, which significantly simplifies their implementation. While geometric controllers achieve acceptable tracking performance at low-to-medium velocities, their accuracy decreases as the vehicle velocity increases, which is due to ignored dynamics, large tire slip, and unmodeled nonlinearities that dominate at high speeds. In this work, we propose an adaptive pure pursuit controller that calculates a variable look-ahead distance based on curvature in a feedforward fashion, complemented by a regulated deviation (error-based) model in the feedback loop, which generates a corrective steering angle that accounts for nonlinearities at higher speeds. A comparative simulation study is presented to demonstrate the superiority of the proposed controller over the traditional pure pursuit controller, which is evidenced by 85.69% improvement in lateral position tracking, 19.75% improvement in yaw angle tracking, and 8% improvement in lap time.

articleTitle: Non-Invasive EEG-Driven Brain-Computer Interface for Motion Control of Assistive Robotics
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Control, Automation, and Instrumentation (IC2AI)
abstract: This study aims to develop a practical proof of implementing a deep learning-based brain-computer interface (BCI) for motion intent classification and control of an assistive robotic arm. A modified version of EEGNet with attention is used for the real-time classification of EEG signals recorded using the Emotiv Epoc X headset. The robotic arm is built on an ESP32-WIFI Arduino. The motor imagery dataset by Physionet used for training consists of four classes out of which two have been used to map right and left arm movements. The data goes through necessary preprocessing steps: down-sampling, Butterworth filter, truncation, and z-score normalization. The modified EEGNet achieves an 82.01% validation accuracy on the dataset. The system has been tested for real-time usability by recordings of 3 seconds at 128Hz with minimum latency.

articleTitle: Path and Trajectory Planning in Unknown Tracks Using Pixy2.1 Camera for Autonomous Racecars
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Control, Automation, and Instrumentation (IC2AI)
abstract: Maintaining maximum allowable speeds throughout a racing track, especially at corners, is essential for competitive performance in autonomous racing. This research integrates computationally-efficient perception and path- and trajectory-planning algorithms, which are suitable for real-time deployment on limited hardware. The algorithms aim is to achieve the global-minimum lap time on an unknown race track by minimizing the summation of locally-minimum times at each track section using a Pixy2.1 camera, which is a fast vision sensor. By processing the vector outputs of the Pixy2.1 camera, smooth track right and left lanes are generated and an optimal race line that minimizes curvature is generated, and an adaptive velocity profile is developed to reach maximum allowable speed at each waypoint along the race line. Experimental testing and validation were conducted on the MR-BUGGY3-KIT car hardware equipped with an RDDRONE-FMUK66 NXP microcontroller. Testing demonstrated the system's ability to generate smooth lane boundaries from the Pixy2.1 camera vectors. Furthermore, the curvature profiles effectively captured the geometric characteristics of the track, facilitating efficient path and trajectory planning while minimizing curvature.

articleTitle: Enhanced Control of an Inverted Cart-Pendulum System Using Cascade PD Controller Optimized with Genetic Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Control, Automation, and Instrumentation (IC2AI)
abstract: The inverted pendulum system is a widely studied benchmark problem in control engineering due to its inherent nonlinearity and instability. In this work, a nonlinear multibody model of the inverted pendulum is developed and analyzed to capture the complex dynamics of the system. A cascade Proportional-Derivative (PD) control scheme is implemented, with the dual objectives of controlling the pendulum angle and the cart position through nested control loops. The optimal tuning of PD gains, a critical factor for robust performance, is performed using Genetic Algorithm optimization technique. The proposed approach is implemented and simulated in MATLAB Simulink with Simscape to evaluate its effectiveness. Simulation results demonstrate the successful control of both pendulum angle and the cart position. The study highlights the success of cascade PD control and superior performance of the GA tuning approach over conventional methods, emphasizing its efficacy in handling nonlinear and dynamic control challenges.

articleTitle: Eco-Bot: Autonomous Solar Panel Cleaner
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Control, Automation, and Instrumentation (IC2AI)
abstract: Eco-Bot (Ecological Robot) is an innovative autonomous solar panel cleaning system aiming to enhance the solar panel efficiency and reduce the environmental impact that conventional methods may cause. Designed for sustainability, Eco-Bot replaces the manual cleaning methods, which need chemical agents, and minimizes the electrical hazards that may occur by navigating autonomously, through solar panel arrays, detecting dirt, and performing effective cleaning. It adapts to various climatic conditions and panel configurations, ensuring thorough and efficient maintenance across diverse solar systems. Enhancing solar panel performance and longevity contributes significantly to the sustainability of renewable energy systems. Eco-Bot utilizes advanced robotics and AI (Artificial Intelligence) to address the persistent issue of dust and debris accumulation. This paper explores the design and operation of the proposed system.

articleTitle: An Analog Hardware Neural Network-Based Classifier for Robot Manipulation
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Control, Automation, and Instrumentation (IC2AI)
abstract: In this work, a fully low-power analog integrated artificial neural network architecture is proposed. The design includes circuits operating in the sub-threshold region, such as the ReLu-based circuit, Gaussian function circuit, analog tunable current mirrors and a current-mode argmax operator. This architecture is evaluated on a Robot Manipulation classification task. The implementation achieves a power consumption of 734 nW and delivers an average accuracy of 86.45%. The design was developed and validated using the TSMC 90nm CMOS process. Furthermore, post-layout results are compared against both software-based implementations and existing solutions in the literature.

articleTitle: PI-Type Sliding Mode Fractional-Order Synchronization of a Memristive Chua Circuit
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Control, Automation, and Instrumentation (IC2AI)
abstract: In this study, a sliding mode fractional-order synchronization is proposed for the memristive chaotic Chua system. After the integer-order model of the chaotic memristive Chua system is given, a PI-type sliding surface-based controller structure combined with the fractional derivative operator is devised. The stability analysis of the synchronization closed-loop system is proven in the sense of Lyapunov theory. To demonstrate the effectiveness and applicability of the proposed controller structure, the fractional-order derivative operator in the controller structure is considered with two different fractional orders, and computer-based numerical simulation studies are performed comparatively.

articleTitle: Advising and Scheduling Tool Based on Electrical Power Engineering Concepts
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Control, Automation, and Instrumentation (IC2AI)
abstract: University administrations are always in need for tools to optimize their operation decreasing operational costs and ensuring a good learning experience for students. Advising and course offering are two main tasks that require knowledge in the field and expertise. The tasks need also data and its related analytics. This paper presents an innovative advising tool based on data mining leveraging from electrical power concepts. The tool uses Python and Excel to automate advising sheets and electrical power engineering by applying simultaneity and the factor of utilization to students records and courses to predict future course enrollment with a RMSE=0.75. The research proposed is unique since it helps administration and advisors. With the reduction of resources and disruption of the classical educational system new tools should be elaborated to reduce costs and secure on time graduation of students.

articleTitle: Lightweight AI Algorithms for Energy-Efficient Signal Fusion, Real-Time Event Detection, and Adaptive Filtering in Heterogeneous IoT Environments
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Control, Automation, and Instrumentation (IC2AI)
abstract: As the number of Internet of Things (IoT) devices increases rapidly, optimizing energy efficiency in resource-constrained environments is crucial for real-time data processing and decision-making. This paper presents the design and implementation of lightweight Artificial Intelligence (AI) algorithms for decentralized signal fusion, real-time event detection, and adaptive filtering in heterogeneous IoT networks. This work aims to reduce energy consumption while maintaining accuracy in data fusion and event detection tasks. We employ Support Vector Machines (SVM) for signal fusion, decision trees for event detection and Reinforcement Learning (RL) for adaptive filtering. Extensive simulations demonstrate significant improvements in both accuracy and energy efficiency, validating the proposed approach as a suitable solution for energy-constrained IoT ecosystems.

articleTitle: Estimating User Gait Intention with a Single-Joint Admittance Model in a 2-DOF Lower Limb Exoskeleton
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Control, Automation, and Instrumentation (IC2AI)
abstract: This paper presents an innovative approach for intention estimation in an exoskeleton (EXOLL1) designed to assist human locomotion. The approach integrates a human effort observer (HEO) based on inverse dynamics model to estimate the patient's effort without using force sensors. An admittance model at the knee joint allows for the estimation of the subject's intention by converting human effort into a reference trajectory. A simple algorithm is integrated into the intention estimation framework for sensorless gait phase detection, facilitating more natural and adaptive gait assistance. Modulation of the admittance parameters allows for gravitational compensation and reduction of the patient's effort. Simulations of the proposed method are performed using a Simscape model of the EXOLL1 prototype and an OpenSim model of a healthy subject. The results show the effectiveness of our approach in accurately estimating the patient's intended movements.

articleTitle: GAIWAP (Gait Analysis to Determine the Improvement of Walking Ability in People with Disabilities)
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Control, Automation, and Instrumentation (IC2AI)
abstract: The use of complex electronic systems in medical technology applications is constantly increasing. These systems are becoming increasingly important, particularly in the area of analyzing the progress of treatment, as they can be used to identify any deficits that may still exist. Although systems are now available from a number of manufacturers, they are not always applicable to all mobile problems, so approaches with adapted system technology must be used.

articleTitle: Liquid Crystal Technology for IoT and Beyond: Advancements and Future Directions
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Control, Automation, and Instrumentation (IC2AI)
abstract: This article presents a focused review of past performance, recent advancements and emerging trends in liquid crystal-based reconfigurable millimeter-wave components and systems, with applications extending to the Internet of Things (IoT) and beyond. Two primary developmental trajectories are highlighted: the use of phasereconfigurable delay lines in passively fed phased-array antennas and reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RIS) to enable adaptive communication, and the implementation of passive tunable filtering for dynamic spectrum allocation. These trends underscore an ongoing shift towards adaptable, intelligent, and energy-efficient hardware solutions, facilitating the next generation of smart, interconnected devices for IoT and AIoT (artificial intelligence of things). Furthermore, the potential of liquid crystal-based multi-modal sensing and communication is proposed and investigated, with a focus on improving power efficiency and enhancing security to support the development of future IoT ecosystems.

articleTitle: IoT Based Energy Management System
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Control, Automation, and Instrumentation (IC2AI)
abstract: The need for efficient energy management solutions has never been more pressing in an era of rising energy consumption and increased environmental awareness. By creating a cutting-edge Energy Management System (EMS) that not only allows users to lower their energy costs but also promotes a healthier environment, this project aims to address this urgent problem. This system's foundation is an Internet of Things (IoT) infrastructure that makes use of Wi-Fi and PIC microcontrollers. This IoT system makes it possible to seamlessly control a variety of endpoints, ensuring optimal energy usage. To balance usage with demand and availability, devices are prioritized according to user preferences and the availability of energy sources. Additionally, by developing a user interface, this project aims to improve the user experience. Users can interact with the energy management system, which offers real-time insights into energy consumption and device control. Users can easily monitor, control, and tailor their preferences for energy use. which encourages greater engagement and control.

articleTitle: Sigma Delta ADC for Automated Selection of Staples in Gastric Sleeve Surgery
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Control, Automation, and Instrumentation (IC2AI)
abstract: The Gastric Sleeve procedure is crucial for combating obesity, promoting weight loss, and improving metabolic health. Despite its effectiveness, the manual selection and placement of staples can lead to complications due to variability in staple size, orientation, and placement. A Sigma-Delta ADC is designed to measure stomach layer thickness and select appropriate staples. The circuit uses a first-order Delta-Sigma modulator with an integrator, a comparator, a D flip-flop, and a 1-bit DAC in a feedback loop. Transient and FFT simulations were conducted, confirming the system's effectiveness.

articleTitle: Design of an Active Tuned Mass Damper (ATMD) and Simulation for Vibration Reduction in Multi-Degree-of-Freedom Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Control, Automation, and Instrumentation (IC2AI)
abstract: This paper presents the development and simulation of an Active Tuned Mass Damper (ATMD) system designed to reduce vibrations in multi-degree-of-freedom (MDOF) structures. The dynamic model was derived using Newtonian mechanics and represented in state-space form to facilitate control design. The developed ATMD system was tested using acceleration records from the earthquake that occurred in Kahramanmaraş on February 6, 2023. Simulation analyses performed with a PID controller showed that the maximum average displacement ratio was reduced by approximately 13.2 percent, and the RMS error value was measured as 0.044. Numerical analyses carried out in the MATLAB Simulink environment showed the effectiveness of the ATMD system in reducing vibrations and making it an efficient solution, especially suitable for large-scale structures like high-rise buildings and long-span bridges. The ATMD system proposed in this paper is effective in minimizing the impact of earthquakes when compared to an uncontrolled counterpart, and all controllers were feasible from an energy expenditure point of view. Results showed that the proposed approach, if deployed, yields effective vibration reduction in realistic scenarios, which enhance the safety of structures, mainly under earthquake-affected loading scenarios.

articleTitle: Kinetic Power Gym: Harnessing Human Energy for Sustainable Fitness
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Control, Automation, and Instrumentation (IC2AI)
abstract: The study explores the use of renewable energy sources, particularly human-produced energy, in gyms. The system aims to create a Gym Slab using customers' motion energy to generate electricity. It uses Footstep Power Generators (FPGs) to convert repetitive motion into a sustainable energy source, raising environmental awareness and demonstrating the relationship between human activity and renewable energy generation. The system's foundation manages data and energy distribution across the different facilities. The network collects, processes, and sends real-time data, providing users with information on their energy contributions and usage habits. As for the operational structure, it is based on “energy transformation”, where each action contributes to the group's effort to power fitness facilities. The system optimizes power distribution using a centralized database management system, encouraging exercisers to become more involved in the community and care for the environment. The proposed system is implemented using mechanical and electrical components and tested for efficiency and durability. During the testing process, various loads are connected, and the overall performance is analyzed to confirm that the generated power met the demands of the connected loads. The system is able to reduce the electrical bill of the gym and an RDI study shows that its price can be covered after being deployed for few months.

articleTitle: Evaluating the Impact of Sampling Strategies on Classification Accuracy in Point-MAE for Point Cloud Classification
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Control, Automation, and Instrumentation (IC2AI)
abstract: Point-MAE is a recently introduced technique for deep learning on point cloud data, and prior research has demonstrated the significant impact of pretraining datasets on the classification downstream task performance. Another critical factor in working with point cloud data is the sampling method and the number of sampling points used. This paper explores different sampling techniques for point cloud data, with a focus on farthest point sampling, as employed in Point-MAE. In this study, Point-MAE is pretrained on two datasets using varying numbers of sampling points (512, 1024, and 2048). Each pretrained model is then fine-tuned with the same sampling densities on four datasets. Results indicate that higher sampling points generally improve classification accuracy. However, pretraining on ModelNet40 with 512 sampling points and finetuning on ScanObjectNN PB_T50_RS variant achieved a classification accuracy of 92.72%. These findings highlight the importance of selecting an optimal pretraining dataset and sampling density based on dataset complexity.

articleTitle: Hybrid Deep Learning Model for QRS Detection and Fourfold Heartbeat Classification
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Control, Automation, and Instrumentation (IC2AI)
abstract: The field of biomedical signal analysis has been developing a wide range of approaches to solve the challenge of developing an automated algorithm for analyzing ECG data to help diagnose cardiac disorders for over a century. The suggested techniques in this paper include a new gradient-based QRS detection algorithm that, when tested against the MIT/BIH dataset, produced a sensitivity of 96.77% and a positive predictivity of 99.81%. For the segmentation and classification of heartbeats, a hybrid deep learning model comes next, with a potential sensitivity of 85.31%, precision of 76.53%, accuracy of 93.52%, and F1-score of 92.87%. These outcomes are on par with the most advanced algorithms.

articleTitle: AI-Driven Robotic Disassembly: Harnessing IoT and Data Collection for Sustainable E-Waste Solutions
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Control, Automation, and Instrumentation (IC2AI)
abstract: The escalating environmental impact of electronic waste poses substantial challenges for sustainable waste management and material reclamation. This study proposes an intelligent robotic disassembly station that integrates Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Internet of Things (IoT) to optimize autonomous e-waste data collection and disassembly processing. The station incorporates a conveyor belt, metal sensor, and a camera attached to a robot to detect and categorize materials in real-time. The idea is to construct a learning-based dataset, enabling the system to recognize and optimize disassembly procedures for unknown waste. Over time, the system enhances efficiency by predicting the disassembly pathway for similar products, reducing time and energy expenditure. The integration of IoT enhances communication between sensors and cloud platforms for real-time monitoring and data storage, ensuring the robot recognizes its environment. Experimental findings demonstrate a significant enhancement in material recovery rates and its precision, contributing to more environmental Solutions.

articleTitle: Enhanced MRAC Design Using Filtered Regressors for Bilateral Pneumatic Teleoperation Control
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Control, Automation, and Instrumentation (IC2AI)
abstract: This paper presents the design of an adaptive controller for a bilateral pneumatic teleoperation system that consists of two linear actuators connected electrically via signals and physically via pneumatic transmission lines. Bilateral control ensures that the slave actuator (follower) traces the position of the master actuator (leader), while transmitting haptic feedback to the operator. The device is designed for application in the medical field within magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) conditions, and is thus subjected to continuously varying operation environments. A model reference adaptive controller (MRAC) is integrated with a filter design that generates smooth and practical regressor estimates, which ensures adaptation to various operating conditions and guarantees stability in all expected environments, while maintaining ideal transparency. The system's performance is validated through numerical simulations using a high-fidelity nonlinear dynamics model, and the obtained results demonstrate fast asymptotic tracking between the master and slave actuators in response to different unknown contact environments.

articleTitle: Real-Time Drone System for Detecting, Tracking, and Following of a Mobile Robot in ROS/Gazebo
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Control, Automation, and Instrumentation (IC2AI)
abstract: Surveillance drones equipped with video transmission capabilities play a crucial role in modern security systems, with the integration of OpenCV for object detection marking a significant advancement. This study evaluates the detecting accuracy by varying the distance between the drone and the target object, addressing gaps in current research through a detailed practical insight. This research explores key aspects of drone-based video surveillance, including object detecting, tracking and real-time following, aiming to enhance understanding and methodology in Computer Vision (CV) applications with Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs). The Simulation of a surveillance drone system in Gazebo simulator within the ROS2 framework. The drone is programmed to dynamically follow and track a mobile robot, enabling systematic analysis of the object detection algorithm's performance. The findings contribute to advancing the reliability and effectiveness of drone-based video surveillance systems for future innovations in security and monitoring applications.

articleTitle: Challenge of Evolution to Cloud-Based Control Systems with Aging Industrial Device Communication Protocols
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Control, Automation, and Instrumentation (IC2AI)
abstract: This paper provides a future looking perspective on the evolution of cloud-native technologies in the design, operation, and maintenance of industrial control systems with aging device communication protocols. First a look at traditional control system design patterns and technologies before the Industry 4.0 shift. Then consider how advanced computing and networking power introduced with Industry 4.0 changed control systems in the past 10 years. Finally, a look at how the shift towards cloud-native technologies, big data processing, AI, and advanced computer-aided learning algorithms are challenged by the data modeling and transport norms of today's systems. This paper is a work in progress and draws no conclusions on the future. The purpose of this paper is to bring academic discussion into the needs for communication standardization in the evolving space of cloud-based control system design.

articleTitle: A Comparative Analysis of Liquid Neural Networks and Incremental Learning Approaches for Stock Market Prediction
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Control, Automation, and Instrumentation (IC2AI)
abstract: Due to the complexity, challenge, and fast growth of stock markets, they encourage more efficient use of financial resources and the expansion of macroeconomics. Tesla and Apple stock prices fluctuate constantly due to the impact of various industries and market conditions. The extraction of previously unknown patterns and information from time series is central to numerous real-world applications. This paper presents a comparative study of stock market prediction techniques for Tesla and Apple stocks, focusing primarily on the application of Liquid Neural Networks (LNN) and evaluating their performance against Incremental Learning methods. Employing LNN, a novel approach in the field of time-series forecasting, we developed models that leverage the dynamic and flexible structure of LNN to adapt to the complex and non-linear patterns observed in stock prices. The performance of the LNN model was quantitatively assessed using standard metrics: Mean Squared Error (MSE), Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE), Mean Absolute Error (MAE), Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE), and Directional Accuracy. The LNN model achieved an MSE of 0.000317, RMSE of 0.0178, MAE of 0.014131, MAPE of 1.8%, and a Directional Accuracy of 49.36%. In contrast, the Incremental Learning approach yielded an MSE of 0.54355, RMSE of 0.73725, MAE of 0.73158, MAPE of 89.39%, and Directional Accuracy of 28.37%. These results underscore the superior accuracy and effectiveness of LNNs in modeling stock market behaviors compared to traditional Incremental Learning methods. The findings not only demonstrate the potential of LNNs in financial analytics but also suggest avenues for further research into enhancing predictive accuracy and model robustness.

articleTitle: Formula 1 Race Winner Prediction Using Random Forest and SHAP Analysis
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Control, Automation, and Instrumentation (IC2AI)
abstract: Predicting the outcomes of Formula 1 (F1) races presents a significant challenge due to the complex interplay of numerous factors, including driver skill, vehicle performance, team strategy, and unpredictable race-day conditions. This paper investigates the application of the Random Forest algorithm enhanced with SHAP (Shapley Additive Explanations) analysis to forecast race winners while providing interpretability to the model's predictions. By leveraging extensive historical data encompassing driver metrics and race conditions, we aim to build a model that achieves high predictive accuracy and offers valuable insights into the most influential factors affecting race outcomes. Our approach demonstrates how integrating machine learning with explainable AI techniques can assist F1 teams in making data-driven decisions, ultimately optimizing their strategies in the highly competitive environment of professional racing.

articleTitle: An End-to-End Pothole Detection and Avoidance System for Autonomous Ground Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Control, Automation, and Instrumentation (IC2AI)
abstract: Contemporary research in autonomous driving has primarily focused on improving perception and planning subsystems to allow vehicles to better perceive and react to environmental uncertainties, but mostly in countries with well-maintained road infrastructures. Given that potholes are common structural road defects, an autonomous vehicle must be able to perceive and plan around potholes to avoid vehicular damage. This paper proposes an end-to-end pothole detection and avoidance system that runs in real-time consisting of an instance segmentation model running on a stereo camera and a path planner designed to execute four different maneuvers: (1) pothole avoidance, (2) alignment between the centers of the vehicle and the pothole, (3) deceleration and slowly passing over the pothole, and (4) stopping before the pothole. The overall system is deployed on an Intel Core i7-97 50H CPU laptop with an NVidia GTX 1650 GPU. All four maneuvers are executed on the NV-X1 platform, and experimental results demonstrate the proposed system's ability to segment pothole instances in 3D, plan an appropriate response maneuver, and successfully execute each maneuver.

articleTitle: Implementation of Safety-Related Intrusion Detection for an Industrial Robotic Arm
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Control, Automation, and Instrumentation (IC2AI)
abstract: Ensuring the safety of human workers collaborating with industrial robots is paramount. This research work presents a novel approach by developing a safety-related intruder detection system for the operational zones of industrial robots, following the IEC 61508 standard and adopting the related redundant architecture. The hardware integrates light curtains and radar sensors in a dual-layer configuration, while the software utilizes a safety system-on-chip to implement real-time diagnostics and fault tolerance. Protecting employees and ensuring a smooth and safe work environment are significant concerns for all companies. As a result, numerous standards and regulations have been established to provide safe collaboration between humans and machines. However, despite these measures, accidents continue to occur, resulting in varying degrees of injuries. The proposed system is depicted through a comprehensive schematic, emphasizing the integration of safety measures within the robotic environment. The detailed prototype demonstrates practical application, show-casing the system's ability to detect intrusions, initiate emergency responses, and transition to fail-safe states during component failures. This research work advances safety protocols in human-robot collaboration within industrial settings, fostering a safe working environment through a well-defined safety framework.

articleTitle: Crone Sky Hook 1G Suspension
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Control, Automation, and Instrumentation (IC2AI)
abstract: In the active vehicle suspensions domain, this paper proposes a controller whose integrating behavior exhibits different orders at low, medium and high frequencies. This proposal meets two objectives. From a control theory point of view, the first objective is the robustness of the stability degree of the control loop with respect to the parametric uncertainties of the sprung mass. From a vibration comfort point of view, the second objective is the minimization of the vertical acceleration of the sprung mass. Due to the existing link with the first-generation CRONE control, this new architecture is called Crone Sky Hook 1G suspension. The results obtained in simulation clearly illustrate the interest of this approach in the frequency and time domains.

articleTitle: Extent of Artificial Intelligence Chatbots' Integration Into Routine Medical Imaging: Exploring the Boundaries of AI Advancements
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Control, Automation, and Instrumentation (IC2AI)
abstract: The integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) chatbots into routine medical imaging offers promising potential to enhance workflow efficiency, reduce errors, and provide real-time assistance to healthcare professionals. This study explores the extent to which AI chatbots can be integrated into medical imaging, specifically radiology, to support professionals in decision-making and patient care. Through the development and testing of an AI chatbot, data was collected from 70 healthcare professionals in various roles. Participants assessed the chatbot's accuracy, precision, effectiveness, and ease of use, overall satisfaction, intention to reuse and comfort through a structured survey. The results showed that over 75% of healthcare professionals who interacted with the chatbot found it to be accurate, precise, effective, and easy to use. Results also showed a significant correlation between the chatbot's performance and users' satisfaction, intention to reuse and comfort. The findings suggest that AI chatbots can significantly contribute to improving the accuracy and efficiency of medical imaging processes, reducing human errors, and enhancing user experience.

articleTitle: Optimal Energy-Efficient Trajectory Planning for Multirotor UAVs
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Control, Automation, and Instrumentation (IC2AI)
abstract: A major limitation of current battery-powered Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) is their finite onboard energy, which restricts both flight duration and the range of missions they can effectively complete. To overcome this challenge and extend flight times, reducing the vehicle's energy consumption is crucial. Various strategies have been explored in the literature to achieve this, including advancements in UAV design and materials, the incorporation of energy-capturing systems, and the development of energy-minimizing control approaches. This work focuses on optimizing control strategies to minimize energy consumption. Specifically, the aim is to improve the efficiency of a hexarotor supplied by a Lithium-Polymer (Li-Po) battery as it follows a designated reference position by introducing innovative high-level energy-saving control techniques. To achieve this, three metaheuristic algorithms are developed to address the optimization problem: Grey Wolf Optimizer, Particle Swarm Optimization and Genetic Algorithm. All methods are implemented and validated using the MATLAB/Simulink simulation environment.

articleTitle: Subterranean Vegetable Sorting with YOLO Models and Flask Framework
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Control, Automation, and Instrumentation (IC2AI)
abstract: The integration of advanced deep learning models, such as YOLOv5 and YOLOv8, into carrot cultivation significantly enhances post-harvest sorting systems, allowing for the effective differentiation between healthy and rotten carrots. This work streamlines the sorting process, ensuring that only high-quality produce reaches the market, thereby providing substantial advantages for traders. By automating this procedure, farmers can improve food safety, monitor shelf life, and enhance customer satisfaction, ultimately increasing productivity and profitability. The system employs convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to analyze visual data captured during harvest or post-harvest stages. These models are trained to identify distinguishing features of carrots, such as color changes, texture anomalies, and shape deformations, resulting in precision rates of 98.3% and 96.4% in identifying freshness with YOLOv8 and YOLOv5 respectively, and 96.5% and 93.6% in detecting rotten. Extensive training and evaluation have demonstrated notable improvements in performance metrics, validating the effectiveness of these models. As a prototype, we have developed a Flask web application for detecting whether carrots are rotten or fresh. This system significantly enhances productivity by allowing for quick and accurate assessment of carrot quality. The adoption of this AI-driven technology marks a transformative step toward optimizing resource management and maximizing crop value in modern agriculture.

articleTitle: Inclusive Communication for Arabic Notation: Decoding Lebanese Sign Language Using Gesture Recognition
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Control, Automation, and Instrumentation (IC2AI)
abstract: Effective communication is indispensable for human connection, learning, and social engagement. However, for those with physical disabilities, particularly the deaf and mute community, verbal communication becomes a significant challenge. Expressing thoughts becomes complicated when sign language, a primary mode of communication for this community, is not widely understood. While devices exist to convert sign language into text and speech, they are predominantly designed for English-spoken people. In this work, we focus on identifying the Arabic hand sign language, a unique and regionally distinctive sign language, that has not garnered much attention from foreign recognition systems. We study the characteristics of the above-mentioned sign language and try to convert it into speech and text. We research, investigate, implement, test, and evaluate an online real-time Arabic Sign Language interpreter based on gesture recognition, as an attempt to revolutionize accessibility for the Lebanese deaf and mute, reducing communication barriers in education, healthcare, and various sectors.
